reference.source: OMIM / GeneReviews / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Most individuals identified by newborn screening or urinary aminoacid patterns remain entirely asymptomatic
Autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in SLC6A19, encoding the neutral amino acid transporter B0AT1 in the small intestine and renal proximal tubule
The biochemical hallmark is a neutral (monoaminomonocarboxylic) aminoaciduria with normal excretion of acidic and basic amino acids
Symptomatic disease resembles pellagra, with a photosensitive skin rash, intermittent cerebellar ataxia and neuropsychiatric features, reflecting tryptophan loss and reduced niacin synthesis
Attacks are often provoked by intercurrent illness, poor nutrition, sunlight exposure or stress
Management centres on a good protein intake and niacin (nicotinamide) supplementation, with attention to precipitating factors
Symptoms are typically episodic and tend to improve with age
Tryptophan malabsorption underlies the niacin deficiency because tryptophan is a niacin precursor
reference.pathophysiology: Hartnup disease results from defective transport of neutral amino acids due to loss-of-function variants in SLC6A19, which encodes the apical neutral amino acid transporter B0AT1 expressed in the intestinal brush border and renal proximal tubule. Impaired transport causes intestinal malabsorption and renal wasting of neutral amino acids, notably tryptophan. Because tryptophan is a precursor for the synthesis of nicotinamide (niacin), its loss can produce a functional niacin deficiency, giving pellagra-like photosensitive dermatitis and neurological features. The unabsorbed amino acids also undergo bacterial degradation in the gut. Adequate dietary protein and niacin supplementation compensate for the losses, and most patients remain asymptomatic because of compensatory absorption of amino acids as small peptides.
additionalDifferentials: Generalised aminoacidurias such as Fanconi syndrome
Other inborn errors presenting with intermittent neurological symptoms
additionalInvestigations: Urine amino acid chromatography showing neutral aminoaciduria
Plasma amino acid profile (often normal or low neutral amino acids)
Assessment of niacin/nicotinamide status where feasible
Exclusion of nutritional or malabsorptive causes of pellagra
redFlags: Severe or recurrent ataxia impairing function
Progressive neuropsychiatric deterioration during an attack
Extensive photosensitive dermatitis with secondary infection
Failure to thrive with poor nutritional intake
reference.prognosis: The great majority of individuals are asymptomatic with a normal life expectancy; symptomatic cases usually respond well to niacin and adequate protein intake and tend to have fewer episodes with increasing age.
pitfalls: Treating a pellagra-like presentation without recognising the underlying transporter defect
Assuming all cases are symptomatic, when most are benign screening findings
Overlooking precipitating factors such as poor nutrition or intercurrent illness
Misinterpreting an isolated aminoaciduria as a generalised tubulopathy
references: Scriver's The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease
